correctness.rationale: In the developed sector let delta be the shorter separation on the angular circle. Its range is [0,alpha], with alpha<pi; the chord in the corresponding wedge stays inside the radial disk. Any path through the apex has length at least r+s; an apex-avoiding path whose lifted angular sweep reaches pi also has length at least r+s, by cutting at its first such angle and using radial distance on the remainder. For smaller lifted separations the planar chord bound and monotonicity in separation give the claimed cosine law. Independent area sampling gives radial moments E[r]=2ell/3, E[r²]=ell²/2, with delta independent and uniform, yielding ell²(1−8 sin(alpha)/(9alpha)). At fixed area the derivative of the normalized function has numerator g=8(2 sin(alpha)−alpha cos(alpha))−9alpha with g''=8alpha cos(alpha); g' rises and then falls with one zero in each half, and g(0)=0, g(pi/2)>0, g(pi)<0 force exactly two interior zeros with the stated signs. The endpoint limits and f(pi/3)<1/pi ensure the smaller zero is the unique global minimizer. Independent numerical bisection agrees with the displayed precision up to last-digit roundoff. Fixed-slant coupling delta=alpha U gives almost sure strict increase for positive radii and U>0. Alpha is half the developed angle, not half the physical apex angle. The supplied simulation was inspected, not executed; it is supplementary, not a proof.
